description: Call this first for any tax, VAT/GST, payroll or filing question about a country or US state, such as "how much tax will I pay in Spain", "do I need to register for VAT", "when is my tax return due", "is this deductible", "how is a freelancer or a company taxed in Germany", "sales tax in Texas" or "what changes if I move to Portugal". Pass the user's question as `intent` and the country or US state as `jurisdiction` ('DE', 'US-TX', 'Florida'). If no place is named, start infers one when the question makes it clear and says so in `jurisdiction_source`. Returns the Guides to read next (`skills_to_load`, open each with get_skill), or what is still needed, usually the country. Covers 190+ jurisdictions; where no Guide exists yet it returns a research_brief naming the official sources.

acting_as.description: Optional. Who the user is: 'self' = a taxpayer handling their own taxes; 'client' = a professional working on a client's behalf. Infer it from the conversation; omit it if unclear.

intent.description: Required. The user's question or goal in their own words, e.g. 'how much tax will I pay as a freelancer', 'VAT return', 'set up a company'.

jurisdiction.description: Country or US state: ISO 2-letter code, US state code or name (e.g. 'MT', 'GB', 'US-CA', 'Florida'). Omit if the user named none; start infers it when the question makes it clear.

reason.description: One sentence, in the user's own words, on what they actually asked for here — captured only to improve routing. E.g. 'user sold ETH and wants to know what to report'. Optional but helpful.

taxpayer_type.description: The taxpayer's occupation, when known. Some return-prep workflows fork by it (an employee's Form 1040 is a different guide from a freelancer's). Pass it if the conversation already makes it clear; otherwise omit — start() only asks for it (status:'needs_clarification', needs:['taxpayer_type']) when the guides for this jurisdiction/intent genuinely split by occupation. 'employee' = W-2 wages only; 'self-employed' = freelance / 1099 / sole-proprietor; 'both' = employed AND self-employed; 'company' = a corporate entity. Don't guess — ask the user one short question if unsure.

name: start
title: Answer a tax question (call first)
